title: Engineering Breadboard Weekly — cross-cut briefing (Nov 10 2026)
notes:
Purpose: quick cross-team rollup for engineering org — highlight risks, ship blockers, and converging action items. This doc is intended as the single-week rollup for sync on 2026-11-10 (Tuesday).

Attendees: Aisha Morgan (chair), Liam Chen, Priya Desai, Marcus Cole, Sophie Nguyen, Diego Ramirez, reps from SRE, Observability, Product (Optimize), Developer Experience.

Agenda:
- Brief status: serving runtime health metrics & incidents
- Rollouts: Dedicated v2 autoscaler canary, Optimize suggestions beta
- Observability telemetry gaps & short-term fixes
- Cross-team requests and blockers
- Action items and owners

1) Serving runtime health snapshot (Liam)
- 7-day p50/p95 token latency: 32ms / 152ms (steady). p99 has a small uptick to ~420ms driven by long-sequence LLMs in a single customer fleet.
- Error rate: 0.24% (5xx), majority are transient CUDA OOMs during larger batched requests from internal load tests.
- Throughput: 18k tokens/s aggregate across hosted clusters.
- Recent mitigation: temporarily reduced default batch size for models with >16k context; this dropped OOM spike by ~70%.
- Open question: Do we make this autoswitching behavior default, or keep as per-customer opt-in? (Decision needed by Nov 17)

2) Incident brief (Marcus)
- Incident: inter-region fallback misroute (Nov 8) caused ~30 minutes of degraded performance for 2 enterprise customers. Root cause: policy fallback table had stale model-compatibility metadata after a partial metadata service restart.
- Postmortem status: draft posted to Confluence; immediate fix applied (metadata store TTL reset + retry backoff).
- Next step: add health-checked metadata regeneration + alert if fallback rate > 0.05% for 10m. (SRE owner: Sophie)

3) Rollout updates
- Dedicated v2 autoscaler (Priya): canary completing on three reserved pools; observed ~12% better utilization and 9% lower avg tail latency for batching-heavy customers. Plan: expand to 15% of traffic on Nov 18 for wider validation.
- Redwood Optimize beta (Diego): initial quantization recommendations on embedding workloads show 2.1x CPU reduction, small quality delta for high-dim embeddings — need more evals before recommending to GA customers.
- Console rollout (DevEx): new per-route cost breakdown is in a behind-flag test; feedback from two pilot customers positive but some concerns about token attribution on function-calls. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/678

4) Observability gaps (Sophie)
- Missing: token-level attribution for fallbacks and cached responses in traces (makes root-cause of latency regressions noisy).
- Temporary fix: add an annotation to traces when cache hit/miss occurs; ETA for deployment: Nov 15.
- Longer-term: metricize prefix-KV hit rate per model & per-route; tracking ticket JIRA-OPT-514.

5) Cross-team asks / blockers
- Product (Optimize) requests: an exportable CSV of per-route cost breakdown for customers (for billing reconciliation). Blocker: backend schema changes required; target delivery for prototype Nov 24. Owner: Diego.
- SRE asks: team-level runbook update for region failover; current runbooks incomplete. Owner: Sophie. 2-week backlog priority.
- Serving runtime asks: feed from model-catalog that includes quantization-friendly flags so runtime can auto-select kernels. Blocker: model onboarding pipeline changes. Owner: Priya.

6) Action items (short list)
- Aisha: coordinate decision on autoswitching behavior (make default vs opt-in). Due: 2026-11-17.
- Priya: prepare rollout plan to expand Dedicated v2 autoscaler to 15% traffic; include rollback steps and SLO checklists. Due: 2026-11-16.
- Sophie: add metadata-regeneration health check + alert for fallback rate; add runbook updates for region failover. Due: 2026-11-18 (health check), 2026-11-24 (runbook).
- Diego: prototype per-route cost CSV export and share sample with billing & pilot customers. Due: 2026-11-24.
- Liam: implement trace annotation for cache hit/miss and run synthetic to validate p99-latency signal clarity. Due: 2026-11-15.

7) Risks & decisions needed
- Decision: default autoswitching to smaller batches for >16k context models (pros: reduces OOMs; cons: may increase latency/cost for some customers). Decision owner: Aisha; deadline Nov 17.
- Risk: rollback complexity if Dedicated autoscaler causes regressed tail latency in edge pools; mitigation: canary expansion with canary-specific SLOs and immediate rollback path.

8) Quick wins / housekeeping
- Agreed: teams will use the `/engineering/breadboard-weekly` Confluence page to post any post-meeting updates rather than creating separate docs.
- Agreed: make the per-route token attribution ticket high priority — aim to have first instrumentation merged by Nov 15.

9) Notes to self / open threads (informal)
- Consider an internal knob: 'latency-preserve-mode' for key enterprise customers where batching is reduced but cost is covered by dedicated commits.
- Check with Sales: communicate the Dedicated v2 autoscaler canary benefits to existing reserved customers as a limited opt-in.

10) Follow-ups & next meeting
- Next cross-cut sync: Tue Nov 17, 11:00 PT. Focus: autoswitch decision and canary telemetry review.

Appendix: useful links
- Incident draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/IR+Nov+8+2026
- Canary logs: s3://redwood-inference-release/artifacts/canary-2026-11-09.log
- Trace PR (cache-annot): https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/223

End of notes.
